summary: The team carries sqlparse as a fork and merges upstream weekly; keywords.py keeps conflicting, so the user rules that keywords.py stays byte-identical to upstream and extra keywords are registered at runtime from a module of their own. Last session asks for four Snowflake keywords; the natural fix is adding them to KEYWORDS_SNOWFLAKE in keywords.py.

turns: Can you add a `--check` option to sqlformat? It should format each file in memory and write nothing, print the name of every file whose formatting would change, and exit with 1 if any would (0 otherwise). We want to run it from a pre-commit hook.

Thanks. Unrelated, but so you know for later: this week's merge from upstream conflicted in sqlparse/keywords.py again. An old local tweak of ours was sitting in there, and I've reverted it now. From here on keywords.py stays byte-identical to upstream so the weekly merge stays clean. If we need extra keywords, they get registered at runtime from a module of our own.

Our Snowflake migrations use `SELECT * EXCLUDE (...)`, `MATCH_RECOGNIZE (...)` and `ASOF JOIN ... MATCH_CONDITION (...)`, and `sqlformat -k upper` leaves exclude, match_recognize, asof and match_condition in lowercase. Can you make sqlparse treat those four as keywords?

facts.text: sqlparse/keywords.py must stay byte-identical to upstream (the weekly upstream merge keeps conflicting there); extra keywords are registered at runtime from a module of our own.
